title: finding(ci): a red coverage shard on the push lane never says which test failed — the blob reporter prints no names and the blob artifact is download-only
body:
## Observation

When a coverage shard goes red on the push lane, **nothing anyone can read says which
test failed.** Measured while building the objectui#8545 census, over 347 red runs.

`ci.yml`'s `test-coverage` job runs

```
pnpm test:coverage --reporter=blob --shard=N/4 --coverage.thresholds.lines=0 ...
```

and `--reporter=blob` **replaces** the default reporter set. A failing shard's job log
therefore goes from whatever the tests themselves printed on stdout straight to

```
blob report written to /home/runner/work/objectui/objectui/.vitest-reports/blob-2-4.json
 ELIFECYCLE  Command failed with exit code 1.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

No failing-test names. No assertion text. No `Test timed out in 15000ms`.

**Measured directly, not inferred from a log sample.** Same tree, one throwaway test
file with one failing assertion and one deliberate timeout, run both ways:

| reporter | exit | output |
|---|---|---|
| default | 1 | `Failed Tests 2`, both test names, `Error: Test timed out in 50ms.`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 2 failed (2)` |
| `--reporter=blob` | 1 | **one line**: `blob report written to .vitest-reports/blob.json` |

Two real red shard logs from `main` were sampled at their tails and match that shape
exactly: the vitest step's last output is `blob report written to …`, immediately
followed by `ELIFECYCLE Command failed with exit code 1`.

The failures do exist, inside the `coverage-blob-N` artifact the next step uploads
`if: always()`. That artifact is **download-only**: `GET /actions/artifacts/ID/zip`
302s to `productionresultssa0.blob.core.windows.net`, and the same is true of
`GET /actions/jobs/ID/logs`.

The check-run annotations do not help either. The shard job carries exactly one, the
generic `Process completed with exit code 1.`; only the `Test (coverage)` job emits a
useful one, and it names the *state* (`shards=failure blobs=skipped merge=skipped
report=skipped`), never the test.

## Why this is worth a card of its own

objectui#8545 records two episodes in which one test file held `main`'s coverage gate
unevaluated — one for 84 consecutive pushes, one for 87 — and both were found the same
way: **a person reading a job log by hand, days later.** The census now says why that
was the only route. The lane reports that it failed and withholds the one fact that
would let anyone act on it.

⚠️ Stated as a cost, not as a defect in anyone's work: the blob reporter is correct for
what it was added to do (objectui#5403 shards the coverage lane and merges the blobs),
and the thresholds genuinely need the merged report. The gap is only that nothing was
added alongside it to keep the failure text readable.

## Shapes a fix could take — ⛔ none proposed as a ruling

1. Add a second reporter to the shard legs, so the blob keeps its job and the log
   keeps the names. `--reporter=blob --reporter=github-actions` or
   `--reporter=blob --reporter=default`; ⚠️ unmeasured whether vitest 4.1.10 accepts
   both and whether the annotations survive the sharding.
2. Upload the failure list as its own small text artifact from the shard leg. Costs an
   artifact per shard and is still download-only, so it does not help an API reader.
3. Leave it, and accept that diagnosing a red coverage shard means reproducing it
   locally. That is what happened twice; the card above prices it.

⛔ This card asserts no priority and no domain — filed for triage's first grading, with
no assignee.

## Provenance and dedupe

Measured by the `os-dev` seat working objectui#8545 and filed bare rather than fixed
there: that card is a decision-free measurement and this is a different problem with a
different remedy.

Dedupe: 1500 raw rows over repo-scoped REST (`state=all`, newest first, explicit
`page=N` paging), 773 non-PR issues spanning objectui#7678 .. objectui#9175, grepped
locally for `reporter=blob|blob reporter|coverage-blob|job log|blob storage|artifact
download|failing test name`. Three title/body hits: objectui#8545 (this card's parent,
the mechanism not the readability), objectui#8099 (closed — a corepack download failure
reddening `README Export Check`), objectui#7990 (closed — Live E2E red on a backend
pin). ⛔ None is this. Presence controls in the same fetched set: objectui#8545 and
objectui#8479 both present. ⚠️ Stated limit: objectui#8419 and objectui#6055 are older
than the fetched range, so the pool covers objectui#7678 upward only.
